rationale: enc-rc4 is a tiny, hot-loop crypto kernel (RC4 KSA/PRGA with byte-level S-box arithmetic), so the priority is instruction-level obfuscation that resists pattern-matching of the S-box swap and keystream XOR without bloating the hot loop: SUB gets the highest weights (cheap, correct, effectively hides the characteristic RC4 op sequence), and IBR follows (indirect branching disrupts static control-flow recovery at modest cost on small basic blocks). SPLIT is favored as a nearly-free diversity/size-friendly transform that also feeds IBR more blocks to randomize. FLA and BCF carry high RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights because flattening and bogus control flow can measurably slow tight per-byte loops and inflate a program whose value is its small footprint, so they should only trigger for functions where the profile strongly justifies them (e.g., KSA, which runs once per key and can tolerate flattening); correctness risk stays low since all passes here are semantics-preserving on this straight-line, pointer-light code. ICALL and IGV sit in the middle: indirect calls and global-variable hiding add meaningful reversing friction for the key/state globals, but ICALL's indirect-call overhead matters if the harness calls PRGA per-byte, so its runtime weight is kept moderately high to gate it.
